topic: The DNA of Space: From Linear Combinations to Bases
target_audience: University students beginning Linear Algebra or advanced high school students

outline.topic: The DNA of Space: From Linear Combinations to Bases
outline.target_audience: University students beginning Linear Algebra or advanced high school students

sections.title: Prerequisites: Vectors as Instructions
sections.content: Briefly recap vectors not just as coordinates, but as 'movement instructions' in space. Introduce the concept of scaling (stretching/shrinking) and adding vectors head-to-tail.
sections.example: Visual: A small Robot Scout on a 2D grid. Vector v = [1, 2] is an instruction to move 1 unit east and 2 units north. Scaling 2v means moving twice that distance.

sections.title: The Recipe: Linear Combinations
sections.content: Define a Linear Combination as the result of scaling two or more vectors and adding them together. It is the fundamental 'arithmetic' of linear algebra. Formula: w = c1v1 + c2v2 + ... + cnvn.
sections.example: Character: An Alchemist mixing 'Vector Potions'. If Potion A moves you Right and Potion B moves you Up, combining 3 drops of A and 2 drops of B creates a new path to a specific destination.

sections.title: The Reach: What is a Span?
sections.content: Introduce 'Span' as the set of ALL possible points reachable through linear combinations of a specific set of vectors. Visualize how two vectors can 'fill' a 2D plane.
sections.example: Animation: Two non-parallel arrows starting at the origin. As the coefficients (c1, c2) vary continuously from negative to positive infinity, watch a 2D plane 'paint' itself into existence across the screen.

sections.title: The Redundancy: Linear Dependence
sections.content: Explain Linear Dependence as 'redundancy'. If one vector in a set can be created by a linear combination of the others, it adds no new 'reach' to the span. Conversely, Linear Independence means every vector provides a unique direction.
sections.example: Scenario: Three drones. Drone A moves North, Drone B moves East. If Drone C moves North-East, it is 'dependent' because A and B could already reach any spot C can. Drone C is redundant.

sections.title: The Goldilocks Set: Defining a Basis
sections.content: Combine the previous concepts to define a 'Basis'. A basis is a set of vectors that: 1. Spans the entire space, and 2. Is linearly independent (no redundancy). It is the 'minimalist toolkit' for a coordinate system.
sections.example: Graphic: Compare a messy room with 10 random directional vectors vs. a clean room with just 'i' (unit x) and 'j' (unit y). The 'i and j' set is a Basis because it's the simplest set that reaches everywhere in 2D.

sections.title: Summary and Geometric Wrap-up
sections.content: Consolidate the 5-minute journey: Linear combinations are the tools, Span is the territory covered, Independence is the lack of waste, and Basis is the perfect, efficient map.
sections.example: Final Animation: A 3D space. Show three independent vectors forming a 3D grid (Basis). Remove one, and the space collapses to a 2D sheet (Span). Show how they are the 'DNA' that defines the dimension.

storyboard.title: Prerequisites: Vectors as Instructions
lecture_lines: Think of vectors as instructions for movement.
Vector v moves us east and north.
Scaling v stretches or shrinks this movement.

storyboard.title: The Recipe: Linear Combinations
lecture_lines: Combine instructions by scaling and adding them.
Scale vector v and w independently.
Their sum is called a linear combination.
Weights determine the contribution of each vector.
This arithmetic builds every path in space.

storyboard.title: The Reach: What is a Span?
lecture_lines: What if we use every possible scaling factor?
All resulting points form the vector's span.
Two non-parallel vectors can span a plane.
Span represents the reach of your set.
Varying coefficients paints the entire reachable space.

storyboard.title: The Redundancy: Linear Dependence
lecture_lines: Some vectors don't add new directions.
If one vector is redundant, they're dependent.
Independent vectors each provide a unique path.

storyboard.title: The Goldilocks Set: Defining a Basis
lecture_lines: A basis is a perfect, efficient toolkit.
It must span the entire target space.
It must also be linearly independent.
No redundant vectors, yet every point reachable.
This minimal set defines the coordinate system.

storyboard.title: Summary and Geometric Wrap-up
lecture_lines: Combinations are tools; Span is the territory.
Independence ensures no wasted movement instructions.
Together, they form the space's unique DNA.
